newsitem.title: USA: AEP Mich. nuke seen at full power Sunday.
newsitem.headline: AEP Mich. nuke seen at full power Sunday.

text.p: American Electric Power Co Inc's 1,020 megawatt Cook nuclear power unit 1 was expected to resume electricity output Saturday morning and reach 100 percent production by late Sunday after an unexpected shutdown last weekend, a company spokesman said.
"We're looking to come back Saturday morning and reach full power Sunday night," spokesman Bill Schalk said Thursday.

The Bridgman, Mich. unit had originally been expected to resume electricity production on September 23, but the restart was postponed to replace several nuclear source detectors in the plant, Schalk said.
"It was a conservative decision to continue the outage, we decided that because we were down anyway we would do this extra work," the spokesman said.
The Cook unit tripped off line early September 22 when lightning hit an offsite transmission system, creating a power surge which automatically shut the unit down.
The Cook 1 unit is operated by Indiana Michigan Power Co, a subsidiary of American Electric Power.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
